prompt:
Sprite sheet for an early 1980s 8-bit home computer game with attribute colour cells: the badger courier from the second reference image, walking to the right, redrawn as tiny hardware sprites. Take only the costume and the proportions from the reference images; drawing style, resolution and colours follow this description. Use the first reference image only for the layout: one row of 6 animation frames of a walk cycle, evenly spaced, same scale, feet on the same baseline, each frame a distinct leg position (contact, down, passing, up, contact, down).

Every frame is exactly 24 pixels wide and 40 pixels tall in the native resolution, drawn with large hard-edged square pixels (each pixel about 10 by 10 image pixels), no anti-aliasing, no blur, no gradients. The sprite is monochrome per horizontal band, as on that hardware: the lit pixels of each 8-pixel-high band have one single colour on solid black. From top to bottom: band 1 (the cap and the ears) bright green #00FF00; band 2 (the head, side view, with a black stripe through the eye, white cheek and a black nose tip) bright white #FFFFFF; band 3 (the long knitted scarf and the shoulders) bright red #FF0000; band 4 (the vest, the parcel under the arm and the satchel) bright green #00FF00; band 5 (the short legs and feet) bright white #FFFFFF. Inside each band, details are shown only by black gaps and one-pixel black lines between lit pixels; the dark grey fur of the legs and arms is drawn as a checkerboard dither of lit and black pixels with a solid lit outline. Bold, readable silhouette with chunky shapes, like a hand-pixelled game character of that time.

Solid pure black background #000000 everywhere around and between the frames, no ground, no shadows, no frame borders, no grid lines.

The badger courier: an original mascot character, a stout, short-legged badger with a broad black-and-white striped face, wearing a dark green peaked cap with a brass button, a dark green vest with pockets over a cream shirt with rolled-up sleeves, a long red knitted scarf, a brown leather satchel on a shoulder strap, and a brown paper parcel tied with string under one arm.

No text, letters, numbers, signatures, watermarks or logos anywhere in the image. No real places, brands, franchises or recognisable characters from existing games or films.

Image format: landscape 3:2.

Loading screen of an early 1980s 8-bit home computer adventure game on cassette, authentic pixel art exactly as that machine could show it. The native picture is only 256 pixels wide; every pixel is a large hard-edged square block (about 6 by 6 image pixels), as if the tiny screen were enlarged without smoothing: no anti-aliasing, no blur, no mixed pixel sizes, no gradients.

The hardware colour rule shapes the whole picture: the screen is a grid of 8 by 8 pixel cells and every cell holds only TWO colours, one ink colour for the drawn pixels and one paper colour behind them. Only these fifteen pure, fully saturated colours exist, use nothing else: black #000000, blue #0000D7, red #D70000, magenta #D700D7, green #00D700, cyan #00D7D7, yellow #D7D700, white #D7D7D7 and the bright versions blue #0000FF, red #FF0000, magenta #FF00FF, green #00FF00, cyan #00FFFF, yellow #FFFF00, white #FFFFFF. There is no orange, no brown, no grey, no pink, no pastel and no dark shade of any colour. Large areas of solid black with thin one-pixel outlines in a single bright colour; colour changes happen in blocky 8-pixel steps; shading only with checkerboard or line dither patterns of exactly two colours. Bold, graphic, high-contrast, like a hand-pixelled cassette loading picture by a professional graphic artist of that time. Few big objects with simple, chunky, readable silhouettes; no texture noise, no speckles.

The sky: black at the top with a few single white pixel stars, then a band of blue and black checkerboard dither, then solid blue, then magenta lines on blue, then a red band, and at the horizon a thin band of bright yellow and red lines (the evening glow; there is no orange). Two long flat clouds drawn as black shapes with magenta outlines. The sea is blue with rows of short cyan dashes and a few bright yellow glints just below the horizon. Strict side view like a stage set, no perspective: the cottage seen straight from the front, the boats exactly in profile, the jetty a flat platform on vertical posts. Stone and wood are drawn as black areas with white, yellow or cyan outlines and joint lines, not as painted textures.

Composition for a wide game screen (the top and bottom of the image will be cropped): keep everything important between 11% and 89% of the image height; above 11% only black sky with stars, below 89% only plain quay paving. The horizon lies at about 42% of the image height. The flat walkable top surface of the quay (black with simple white outlines of a few large stone slabs) is a band across the whole width from about 70% of the image height downwards; characters will walk on it. The harbour-master's cottage stands on the left at the back edge of the quay, about 24% of the image width, its door at quay level, one window filled with flat bright yellow; the top of its chimney at about 20% of the image height. The lighthouse stands on a simple rocky headland at the right edge, white with one red band, its top at about 15% of the image height. In the middle a short wooden jetty on posts and the two small boats in profile on the calm water. Along the back edge of the quay: two barrels and a stack of two crates next to the cottage, a coil of rope near the right, and the iron lantern on its wooden post at about 58% of the image width; the middle of the quay surface stays free. The lighthouse lamp only as a small bright yellow spot without any beam, rays or glow, and no smoke from the chimney, no birds (light, smoke and gulls are animated separately in the game). Not a photograph, not a 3D render, not a painting, not modern high-resolution pixel art, not a 16-bit look with many shades, no lens flare, no bloom, no light rays.

Location: the small harbour of Lornholm, a fictional island in a northern sea, at dusk. A stone quay with a short wooden jetty runs along the lower third of the picture. Two small wooden fishing boats are moored at the jetty. On a rocky headland on the right stands a white lighthouse with one red band, its lamp lit. On the left a small stone harbour-master's cottage with a lit window and a smoking chimney. On the quay: two barrels, a stack of crates, a coil of rope and an iron lantern on a wooden post. Calm sea, low clouds, a band of orange light at the horizon, the first stars.

Leave the quay in the foreground free of characters: it is a game background, characters are added later as separate sprites.

No text, letters, numbers, signatures, watermarks or logos anywhere in the image. No real places, brands, franchises or recognisable characters from existing games or films.

Image format: landscape 3:2.
